as_read: Trials used standardized isoflavone extracts with conflicting hot-flush results; the labels print unstandardized aerial-part or herb amounts, with no isoflavone content on the red clover row, and no trial of that material met rule 2.

quote.text: Although the study provides some evidence for a biological effect of Promensil, neither supplement had a clinically important effect on hot flashes or other symptoms of menopause.

proposed_decision_text: These labels print red clover aerial part or aerial parts extract at 1000 mg, red clover extract at 1500 mg, red clover blossom and herb at 800 mg, and one row with no amount; the red clover row states no isoflavone content, and only the 800 mg blossom and herb labels print a purpose, women's health. The trials read used products defined by isoflavone content. The ICE trial gave Promensil, 82 mg isoflavones a day, or Rimostil, 57 mg a day, to 252 women; hot flash frequency, the primary outcome, fell similarly with both and placebo, and the authors found no clinically important effect (12851275). Cochrane found no significant difference between Promensil and placebo in pooled trials and no conclusive evidence for phytoestrogen supplements (24323914). Other meta-analyses of isoflavone extracts report a modest reduction (33920485, 42269521), a larger one limited to Promensil at 80 mg/day in three studies (28160855), and a reduction at 3 to 4 months that didn't persist at 12 months (25074017). 39254422 gave 40 mg isoflavone twice daily with no primary outcome named. Rimostil 50 mg had no effect on bone density and lowered LDL (25369831). 26265926 was 150 mL of extract with 37.1 mg isoflavones, on bone. 33761143 gave 1.91 g of extract as a test food to 36 people for blood glucose with no primary outcome named. No study read tested an unstandardized aerial-part or blossom extract at the amounts on these labels. The evidence is conflicting and doesn't reach the material these labels print; no credit. Abstracts only.
stored_rating_note: positive_moderate rests on 33920485, which pools isoflavone extracts at 37.1-160 mg/day with a figure of 87.34% that the abstract labels homogeneity and the stored record calls high heterogeneity; the ICE trial and Cochrane conflict with it, and none of the pool matches what the labels print.
clinician_items: 31975316: premenopausal women with ER-positive breast cancer on tamoxifen, Promensil Forte 80 mg for 24 months; endometrial thickness stayed constant, breast density fell in both groups, and serum effects on cell lines did not differ. No between-group benefit on menopausal score (p = 0.69).
unread_notes: Abstracts only. 12851275 did not appear in the part of the search lists I read; I opened it directly by PMID and its content confirms the ICE trial. Not opened: 38189863, 26693407, 25263312, 31883666, 30269660, 37836449, 28591133, 33238442, and older trials of Promensil and Rimostil; second search listed 15 of 84, so a preparation match in an unopened older trial can't be excluded. Label 80295 has 9 actives and no amount on the red clover row.
